programs.haiku:
"""Layer-1 MLP down-projection component 3840: the end-of-turn detector.

The component writes a strong, nearly constant signal into the residual stream exactly
when the current token is the chat-template end-of-message marker <|im_end|> (the token
that closes a user or assistant message, including the ones closing tool-call and
tool-response blocks). On a sample of training rows every <|im_end|> fires at about 1.9
(10th-90th percentile 1.7 to 2.1). Every other token is near 0 (std about 0.05), with
small positive blips on some tokens such as '</think>' (about 0.3); the program ignores
those, because they add almost nothing to the variance explained.
"""

READS = ()

END_OF_TURN = "<|im_end|>"
LEVEL = 1.9  # typical activation on an end-of-turn token


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    value = LEVEL if prefix.token_strings[-1] == END_OF_TURN else 0.0
    return carry, value

programs.sol:
"""Approximate a pause to reconsider or introduce a line of thought.

The strongest cues are 'Wait', 'Hmm', 'hold on', and verbs in 'let me ...'.
Smaller cues mark possibilities and alternative approaches. A fading memory
of those cues boosts their punctuation; ordinary text stays near zero.
This is a phrase-based approximation, not a general detector of reasoning.
"""
import re

READS = ()
HESITATION = {'hmm', 'hm', '嗯', '唔'}
REALIZATION = {'ah', 'aha', 'oh', 'oops', '哎', '啊'}
UNCERTAINTY = {'maybe', 'perhaps', 'possibly'}
THINKING = {'think', 'thinking', 'imagine', 'visualize', 'consider',
            'reconsider', 'ponder', 'reflect', 'clarify'}
INSPECTION = {'look', 'check', 'verify', 'examine', 'review'}
SETUP = {'write', 'denote', 'define', 'set', 'use', 'formalize', 'derive',
         'calculate', 'compute', 'solve', 'outline', 'explain'}
EXPOSITION = {'following', 'namely', 'reasoning'}
APPROACH = {'idea', 'thought', 'approach', 'method', 'way'}
IDEAS = {'idea', 'ideas', 'solution', 'approach', 'possibility', 'alternative'}
BASE_CUES = (
    (HESITATION, 1.32), (REALIZATION, 0.132),
    (UNCERTAINTY, 0.624), (THINKING, 0.312),
    (INSPECTION, 0.018), (SETUP, 0.036),
    (EXPOSITION, 0.21), (IDEAS, 0.107),
    ({'see'}, 0.013), ({'try', 'attempt'}, 0.044),
    ({'suppose'}, 0.757), ({'considering'}, 0.485),
    ({'actually'}, 0.336), ({'follows'}, 0.467),
    ({'alternatively'}, 0.604),
)
INVITATION = re.compile(
    r"\blet(?: me|['’]s)(?: (?:just|first|also|now|try to))?\s*$", re.I)
REPEAT_THOUGHT = re.compile(
    r'\b(think|check|consider|see|read)\b[^.!?]{0,45}$', re.I)
THIS_THOUGHT = re.compile(
    r'\b(consider|clarify|see|think about|think of it)\s*$', re.I)
NEW_APPROACH = re.compile(
    r'\b(another|alternative|following)\b[^.!?]{0,40}$', re.I)


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    if carry is None or carry[0] != doc:
        carry = (doc, '', '', 0., 0.)
    _, previous, text, thought, recent = carry
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    word, prev = token.strip().lower(), previous.strip().lower()
    upper = token.strip()[:1].isupper()
    value = -0.001
    for words, strength in BASE_CUES:
        if word in words:
            value += strength
    if word == 'wait': value += 1.504 + 0.98 * upper
    if word in REALIZATION: value += 0.401 * upper
    if word == 'alternatively': value += 0.324 * upper
    if word == 'well' and upper: value += 0.181
    if word in {'okay', 'ok'} and upper: value += -0.013
    if word == 'let':
        value += 0.17 + 0.205 * upper + 1.637 * recent
    if word == 'hold': value += 0.104 + 1.697 * recent
    if word == 'no' and (upper or prev in {'oh', 'wait'}): value += 0.077

    # A proposal to investigate, rather than a statement such as 'I think'.
    invitation = bool(INVITATION.search(text))
    if invitation and word not in {'me', "'s", '’s'}:
        if word in THINKING: value += 2.393
        elif word == 'see': value += 2.111
        elif word in INSPECTION: value += 0.53
        elif word in {'try', 'attempt'}: value += 0.958
        elif word in SETUP: value += 0.719
        elif word.isalpha(): value += 0.426
    if word == 'think' and prev == 'i': value += -0.5
    if word == 'think' and prev == 'to': value += 0.385
    if word == 'me' and prev == 'let': value += -0.187
    if word in {"'s", '’s'} and prev == 'let': value += -0.205
    if word in {'of', 'about'} and prev in THINKING: value += 0.909
    if word in {'at', 'into'} and prev == 'look': value += 0.383
    if (word == 'sup' and upper) or (word == 'pose' and prev == 'sup'):
        value += 0.578  # 'Suppose' split across tokens.
    hold_on = word == 'on' and prev == 'hold'
    correction = word == 'no' and bool(re.search(r'\bwait[,\s]*$', text, re.I))
    again = word == 'again' and bool(REPEAT_THOUGHT.search(text))
    this = word == 'this' and bool(THIS_THOUGHT.search(text))
    new = word in APPROACH and prev in {'another', 'alternative', 'following'}
    if hold_on: value += 2.126
    if correction: value += 2.223
    if again: value += 1.625
    if this: value += 0.67
    if new: value += 0.959
    if word == 'way' and prev in {'this', 'another', 'following'}:
        value += 0.36
    if word == ':' and prev in APPROACH and NEW_APPROACH.search(text):
        value += 1.662

    # Pauses after cues, including a weaker effect at a line break.
    punctuation = bool(word) and all(not c.isalnum() for c in word)
    if punctuation:
        if prev == 'wait':
            value += -0.1 if '\n' in token else 2.143
        if prev in HESITATION: value += 0.292
        if prev in REALIZATION: value += 0.205
        if prev == 'alternatively': value += 0.371
        if prev in {'okay', 'ok', 'well'} and previous.strip()[:1].isupper():
            value += 0.347
        if word.startswith(('.', '!', '?')): value += 0.669 * thought
        elif word.startswith(':'): value += 0.514 * thought
        elif word.startswith(','): value += 0.449 * thought
    elif prev in {'wait', 'hmm', 'oh', 'ah', 'alternatively'}:
        value += 0.258
    if word in UNCERTAINTY: value += 0.434 * recent

    # Two fading memories: a short phrase and a longer sentence.
    cue = 0.
    if word == 'wait' and (upper or prev not in {'can', "n't", 'to'}): cue = 1.5
    if word in HESITATION or word == 'alternatively': cue = 1.
    if word in REALIZATION or word in UNCERTAINTY: cue = .6
    if word == 'let' and upper: cue = .5
    if invitation and word.isalpha() and word != 'me': cue = 1.
    if word in EXPOSITION: cue = max(cue, .6)
    if hold_on or correction: cue = max(cue, 1.5)
    if new or word == 'follows': cue = max(cue, 1.)
    if again or this or (invitation and word in THINKING): cue = max(cue, 2.)
    if word in THINKING and prev != 'i': cue = max(cue, .6)
    thought = max(thought * .94, cue)
    if punctuation and word.startswith(('.', '!', '?', ':')): thought = 0.
    recent = max(recent * .8, cue)
    return (doc, token, (text + token)[-160:], thought, recent), float(value)

"""Sparse Indonesian word-piece responses, not a general language detector.

Nearby grammatical words establish Indonesian rather than English context.
Short ter-/di- pieces are negative; per- noun-forming pieces, -an and short
am/em spellings are positive. Split -nya and quote-closing commas are
negative. Prefix/syllable effects carry into following fragments, strongest
on isolated consonants and weaker on longer pieces. Other activity is not
modeled.
"""
READS = ()
INDONESIAN = frozenset('yang ini itu untuk dengan tidak adalah dari dalam pada '
    'akan sebagai juga karena oleh atau sudah tetapi kepada dapat bukan jika '
    'telah menjadi hanya seperti harus lebih sangat masih bisa saya mereka '
    'kami kita anda banyak sehingga namun bahwa setiap setelah semua selalu '
    'sebuah'.split())
ENGLISH = frozenset('the and of to is for with that a in are from by on '
                    'this it was as be at'.split())
# (Response on this piece, spillover to the following piece.)
PREFIX = {'ter': (-4.4, -3.3), 'di': (-0.8, -0.7),
          'per': (0.4, 0.8), 'pers': (2.7, 1.0), 'pert': (1.7, 0.0)}
FUNCTION = {'yang': -0.9, 'dari': -0.4, 'dalam': 0.6}


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    if carry is None or carry[0] != doc:
        carry = (doc, 0.0, '', 0.0)
    _, evidence, previous_letter, spill = carry
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    piece = token.strip().lower()
    start = token[:1].isspace() or not previous_letter
    evidence *= 0.995
    if token.startswith('<|'):
        evidence, spill = 0.0, 0.0
    marker = piece in INDONESIAN
    if piece == 'yang' and not token.strip().islower():
        marker = False  # A capitalized Yang can also be a surname.
    if start and marker:
        evidence = min(3.0, evidence + 1.0)
    if start and piece in ENGLISH:
        evidence = max(0.0, evidence - 0.7)
    gate = min(1.0, max(0.0, evidence - 0.5))
    response, following = 0.0, 0.0
    if piece.isascii() and piece.isalpha():
        if start:
            response, following = PREFIX.get(piece, (FUNCTION.get(piece, 0.0), 0.0))
            if piece.startswith('ter') and len(piece) == 4:
                response, following = -3.4, -1.4
            if piece.startswith('di') and len(piece) == 3:
                response, following = -1.5, 0.0
            if piece == 'yang' and token.strip()[0].isupper():
                response = -2.0
        elif piece == 'an':
            response = 0.6
        short_m = len(piece) <= 4 and piece.count('m') == 1
        nasal_ending = piece.endswith(('am', 'em', 'ama'))
        nasal_extension = piece in ('aman', 'amb', 'emb', 'emp')
        if short_m and (nasal_ending or nasal_extension):
            response += 2.5
            following = 0.5
        if piece == 'ya' and previous_letter == 'n':
            response = -1.4
        if not start:
            # Tiny consonant fragments retain the prefix effect most strongly.
            n = len(piece)
            scale = 2.0 if n == 1 and piece not in 'aeiou' else 1.0
            if n >= 3:
                scale = 0.75 if n == 3 else (0.3 if n == 4 else 0.1)
            response += scale * spill
            following += 0.5 * scale * spill
    if piece in (',"', ',”'):
        response = -3.5
    letter = token[-1:].lower()
    if not (letter.isascii() and letter.isalpha()):
        letter = ''
    return (doc, evidence, letter, following), gate * response
programs.haiku:
"""Indonesian verb-affix detector for one MLP direction in layer 1.

On Indonesian text the component is strongly negative inside words that start
with the Indonesian prefix "ter-" (terjadi, tersebut, terus), mildly negative on
words starting with "di-" (dibuat, diri) and on the relative pronoun "yang", and
mildly positive on words starting with the prefixes "be-", "pe-", "ke-", "se-",
"de-". Outside Indonesian text it is near zero, and everything else is predicted 0.

Language is judged from the last few words: a word counts as Indonesian when
wordfreq ranks it more common in Indonesian than in English.
"""
from collections.abc import Mapping
from functools import lru_cache

import regex
from wordfreq import zipf_frequency

READS: tuple[str, ...] = ()

# Typical activation for each word class, inside Indonesian text.
PREFIX_VALUES = {"ter": -3.0, "di": -0.6, "be": 0.4, "pe": 0.4, "ke": 0.4, "se": 0.4, "de": 0.4}
WORD_VALUES = {"yang": -1.0}
WINDOW = 12  # recent words used to judge the language


@lru_cache(maxsize=None)
def is_indonesian(word: str) -> bool:
    idn, eng = zipf_frequency(word, "id"), zipf_frequency(word, "en")
    return idn >= 2.0 and idn > eng


def word_value(word: str) -> float:
    if word in WORD_VALUES:
        return WORD_VALUES[word]
    return PREFIX_VALUES.get("ter" if word.startswith("ter") else word[:2], 0.0)


def step(carry, prefix, upstream: Mapping):
    doc = prefix.document_ids
    start = len(doc) - 1
    while start > 0 and doc[start - 1] == doc[-1]:
        start -= 1
    text = "".join(s or "" for s in prefix.token_strings[max(start, len(doc) - 80) :]).lower()
    word = regex.search(r"\p{L}*$", text).group()  # the word so far, ending at this token
    words = regex.findall(r"\p{L}+", text[: len(text) - len(word)])[-WINDOW:]
    if not words or sum(is_indonesian(w) for w in words) <= len(words) / 2:
        return carry, 0.0
    return carry, word_value(word)

programs.sol:
"""Approximate a negative response to nouns for people and their roles.

WordNet's primary noun sense and person-sense share supply the semantics.
Plural frequencies help reject names and rare person readings. Local noun
modifiers, possession, pluralization and code markers adjust the response.
CC-CEDICT applies the same person-noun test to short Han words. State resets
at document boundaries and keeps only bounded local history.
"""
import re
from functools import lru_cache
import regex
import wordnet
import wordfreq
import inflect
import cedict

READS = ()
PLURALS = inflect.engine()
ROLE_WEIGHTS = {
    'worker': -0.08,
    'leader': -0.25,
    'associate': -0.31,
    'adult': -0.06,
    'inhabitant': -0.16,
}
FUNCTION_WORDS = set((
    'a an the this that these those some any no each every all both another '
    'other of to in on at by for from with as into upon and or but nor than '
    'if while because is are was were be been being am have has had do does '
    'did can could would should will shall may might must not'
).split())
POSSESSIVES = set('my your his her its our their whose'.split())
HUMAN_WORDS = set('person people man woman boy girl human men women'.split())


def clip(x, lo, hi):
    return max(lo, min(hi, x))


@lru_cache(maxsize=32768)
def person_noun(word):
    # The fixed WordNet table orders noun meanings by their frequency.
    table = wordnet._wordnet().synsets
    senses = [table[s].category for s in wordnet._synsets(word, 'n')]
    if not senses or senses[0] != 'noun.person':
        return 0.0, 0.0
    forms = wordnet.base_forms(word, 'noun')
    base = next((w for w in forms if w != word), word)
    plural = PLURALS.plural_noun(base) or base + 's'
    capital_plural = PLURALS.plural_noun(base.title()) or plural
    frequency = wordfreq.zipf_frequency(base, 'en')
    plural_frequency = max(wordfreq.zipf_frequency(plural, 'en'),
                           wordfreq.zipf_frequency(capital_plural, 'en'))
    if frequency < 1 or plural_frequency < 0.5:
        return 0.0, 0.0
    common = clip((plural_frequency - frequency + 2) / 0.75, 0, 1)
    value = -0.01 - 0.36 * senses.count('noun.person') / len(senses)
    value += 0.09 * clip(5.5 - frequency, 0, 3)
    value += 0.12 * (word != base)
    for role, weight in ROLE_WEIGHTS.items():
        value += weight * wordnet.is_a(word, role)
    return common * value, common


@lru_cache(maxsize=8192)
def qualifier(word):
    return bool(word and word not in FUNCTION_WORDS
                and word not in POSSESSIVES
                and wordnet.parts_of_speech(word) & {'noun', 'adjective'})


def human_head(word):
    return word in HUMAN_WORDS or person_noun(word)[1] > 0.25


@lru_cache(maxsize=16384)
def person_gloss(gloss):
    gloss = re.sub(r'\([^)]*\)', '', gloss).lower().strip()
    if not gloss or gloss.startswith((
        'to ', 'surname ', 'cl:', 'variant ', 'see ', 'used ',
        'prefix ', 'suffix ', 'classifier ', 'particle ', 'abbr.'
    )):
        return False
    for part in gloss.split(';'):
        words = re.findall('[a-z]+', part)
        if words and human_head(words[-1]):
            return True
        if (len(words) > 1 and words[1] in ('of', 'who', 'engaged', 'in')
                and human_head(words[0])):
            return True
    return False


@lru_cache(maxsize=32768)
def han_word(word):
    glosses = cedict.glosses(word)
    if not glosses:
        return None
    glosses = [g for g in glosses
               if not g.startswith(('CL:', 'variant of'))]
    return sum(map(person_gloss, glosses)) / max(1, len(glosses))


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    old, before, code_history, tail, last = '', '', (), b'', ''
    if carry is not None and carry[0] == doc:
        _, old, before, code_history, tail, last = carry
    text = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    raw = prefix.token_bytes[-1]
    joined_word = old + text
    matches = list(re.finditer('[A-Za-z]+', joined_word))
    word = ''
    if matches and matches[-1].end() == len(joined_word):
        word = matches[-1].group().lower()
        if len(matches) >= 2:
            before = matches[-2].group().lower()
            separator = joined_word[matches[-2].end():matches[-1].start()]
            if '\n' in separator:
                before = ''
    else:
        before = ''
    value, common = person_noun(word) if word else (0.0, 0.0)
    continued = bool(old and text and text[0].isalpha())
    value += common * (-0.38 * continued - 0.23 * qualifier(before)
                       - 0.39 * (before in POSSESSIVES)
                       - 0.22 * (before in ('a', 'an'))
                       + 0.23 * (sum(code_history) >= 2))
    if last == '<|im_start|>':
        value = 0.0  # Protocol role labels are not references to people.
    marker = bool(re.search(
        r'[{}=]|\b(def|class|return|import|function|const|var|public|private)\b',
        text))
    code_history = (code_history + (marker,))[-16:]
    joined = tail + raw
    han = regex.search(r'\p{Script=Han}+\Z', joined.decode('utf-8', 'replace'))
    if han:
        end = han.group()[-4:]
        for length in range(len(end), 0, -1):
            fraction = han_word(end[-length:])
            if fraction is None:
                continue
            value -= fraction * (0.75 if length > 1 else 0.41)
            value -= 0.04 * (fraction >= 0.5 and length > 1)
            value -= 0.11 * (length > len(text) and fraction >= 0.5)
            break
    carry = (doc, word[-50:], before, code_history, joined[-24:], text)
    return carry, float(value - 0.001)

programs.haiku:
"""Layer-1 MLP down_proj component 3844: a git-diff and C-header detector.

The component fires on the token that completes a fixed header line:

* git unified diffs: "+++" starting a line (after a newline) is about 3.9,
  the " b" in "+++ b/path" is about 7.7, and the " a" in "--- a/path" is about 0.9.
* C include guards: "#define" at the start of a line (after "#ifndef X") is about 8.

The values are the mean activations seen in training text, scaled by 0.5, since
the eval rows show the full-size predictions overshoot. Every other position
predicts 0. The program is a few phrase rules; it explains only the part of the
variance that sits on these header tokens.
"""

READS = ()

# phrase -> activation at the phrase's last token (before the 0.5 scale)
PHRASES = {
    "\n+++": 3.9,
    "+++ b": 7.7,
    "--- a": 0.9,
}
KEEP = 80  # characters of recent text carried between steps


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    new_doc = len(prefix.document_ids) < 2 or prefix.document_ids[-1] != prefix.document_ids[-2]
    text = "" if (carry is None or new_doc) else carry
    text = (text + prefix.token_strings[-1])[-KEEP:]
    value = 0.0
    for phrase, act in PHRASES.items():
        if text.endswith(phrase):
            value = act
    if text.endswith("\n#define"):
        value = 8.0
    return text, 0.5 * value

programs.sol:
"""A conviction/victory spelling detector with a smaller legal-guilt response.

The largest values mark convict-/evict- words and their split spellings.
Related vic-/vinc- words and a vowel fragment following v or c also respond;
several other letter endings after v, qu, cu or gu have the opposite sign.
Guilt words (including Chinese 罪) and paired middle dots are separate cues.
Numbers are approximate training means; context and rare spellings remain
unmodeled. Carry retains the current word and a short text tail, resetting
at document boundaries.
"""
READS = ()

import re

LETTER_END = re.compile(r'[^\W\d_]+$')

# Short i-spellings completing a word that currently ends in v or c.
AFTER_V = {
    'iv': 1.865, 'in': 2.182, 'itt': 6.984, 'ict': 10.093,
    'it': 0.73, 'inn': 4.339, 'ind': 2.196, 'inc': 8.938,
    'int': 1.382, 'ic': 1.329,
}
AFTER_C = {'inc': 3.267, 'itt': 4.884, 'int': 0.229, 'inn': 2.901}


def activation(before, token, recent=''):
    s = token.strip().lower()
    # Whether these letters continue the preceding word.
    joined = bool(before and token and token[0].isalpha())
    w = (before + token.lower()) if joined else s
    if s == '罪': return 5.552
    if s == 'tội': return 2.743
    if s == '··': return -1.126
    if s == 'guilty':
        if re.search(r'\bfound(?:\s+\w+){0,3}\s*$', recent):
            return 9.545
        return 3.806
    if s == 'guilt': return 1.158
    if s.startswith('innocen'): return 0.493
    if s == 'verdict': return 2.21
    if s == 'sentenced': return 1.436
    if s.startswith('acquitt'): return 3.219
    if re.search(r'(?:con|e)vict(?:ion[s]?|ed|s)?$',w):
        return 9.576 if joined else 6.871
    if joined:
        if s == 'vinc' and before.endswith('con'): return 7.908
        if s == 'vic' and before.endswith('v'): return 6.734
        if s.startswith('ct') and before.endswith(('ví','vi')): return 6.745
        if s == 'ic' and before == 'v': return 6.734
        if s == 'it' and before.endswith('acqu'): return 4.987
        if before.endswith('v'):
            if s in AFTER_V:
                return AFTER_V[s]
            if s in ('ill','iller','ign','ix','ie','ise'):
                return -1.34
        if before.endswith('c') and s in AFTER_C:
            return AFTER_C[s]
        if before.endswith(('qu','cu','gu')):
            if s in ('ill','il','iller'): return -1.852
            if s in ('ix','ine','ines','ay','ail','ium','ise','ie','ais'):
                return -1.948
        if s in ('qu','inqu') and before.endswith(('cin','quin','qu')):
            return 6.068
        if s == 'qu' and before.endswith(('con','ac','vas','ein')):
            return 2.153
        if s.startswith('vol') and before.endswith('coin'): return 3.816
        if s == 'in' and before.endswith(('vacc','vic','iv')):
            return 3.426
        if before.endswith(('vin','vinc','inc','convin','convinc')):
            if s.startswith(('cent','cen','ces','zione','ere','ing','en','ito','ita')):
                return 3.352
        if before.endswith('vict'):
            if s == 'or': return 6.531
            return 0.681
        if before.endswith(('conviv','convain')): return 4.25
    if s.startswith('convinc'): return 2.273
    if s.startswith('convin'): return 2.546
    if s.startswith('victor'):
        if s == 'victor': return 4.722
        return 0.943
    if s.startswith('victim'): return 0.823
    if s in ('vict','víct'): return 2.462
    if s in ('vinc','vince','vincent'):
        if s == 'vincent': return 2.939
        return 2.151
    if s in ('vic','víc'): return 1.843
    if s == 'vin': return 0.421
    if s.startswith('vit'): return 0.065
    if s == 'vacc': return 1.938
    if s == 'quin': return 1.234
    if s.startswith(('вик','вин','він')): return 1.146
    return 0.0


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    document = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    if carry is None or carry[0] != document:
        before, recent = '', ''
    else:
        _, before, recent = carry
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    value = activation(before, token, recent)

"""Approximate negative pulses on short katakana spelling pieces.

The pulse is strongest at a spelling's beginning and fades over subsequent
pieces. Length and Japanese word frequency soften it. Vowels, final nasal
'n', final 'ru', small vowels, and split UTF-8 characters adjust its size.
Secondary rules cover hiragana 'n', Chinese transcription 'er',
and the colon in a document-initial 'Title:' header. Everything else is zero.

import codecs
import math
import unicodedata
import regex
from wordfreq import get_frequency_dict

KATAKANA = regex.compile(r'\p{Script=Katakana}')
JAPANESE_FREQUENCY = get_frequency_dict('ja')
VOWELS = frozenset('アイウエオ')
SMALL_VOWELS = frozenset('ァィゥェォ')
INITIAL_BY_LENGTH = (-3.7, -2.6, -1.2, -0.8)


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    if carry is None or carry[0] != doc:
        carry = (doc, codecs.getincrementaldecoder('utf8')('replace'), 0, '', 0)
    _, decoder, run, previous, position = carry
    fragment = bool(decoder.getstate()[0])
    decoded = decoder.decode(prefix.token_bytes[-1])
    decoded = unicodedata.normalize('NFKC', decoded)
    text = decoded.strip()
    if decoded and decoded[0].isspace():
        run = 0
    stage = min(run, 2)
    is_kana = bool(KATAKANA.search(text)) or text == 'ー'
    value = 0.0
    if is_kana:
        n = len(text)
        if stage == 0:
            frequency = 9 + math.log10(JAPANESE_FREQUENCY.get(text, 1e-9))
            value = INITIAL_BY_LENGTH[min(n, 4) - 1] + 0.22 * (frequency - 4)
        else:
            value = -(1.7 if stage == 1 else 0.65) / n
        if text.endswith('ン'):
            value -= 0.7
        if text.endswith('ル'):
            value += (-0.7, -2.4, -0.5)[stage]
        if text in VOWELS:
            value += (-1.3, -0.6, -0.5)[stage]
        if text in SMALL_VOWELS and stage:
            value -= 1.5
        if text == 'ッ':
            value -= 0.6
        if fragment:
            value += (-1.1, 0.0, -0.8)[stage]
        value = min(value, 0.0)
    elif decoder.getstate()[0].startswith((b'\xe3\x82', b'\xe3\x83')):
        value = -0.7  # An unfinished Japanese character.
    elif text == 'ん':
        value = -1.7
    elif text == 'っ':
        value = -0.6
    elif text.endswith(('尔', '爾')):
        value = -3.0  # The 'er' character used in foreign-name transcriptions.
    if position == 0:
        value = 0.0
    if position == 1 and previous == 'Title' and text == ':':
        value = -20.8
    if decoded:
        if decoded[-1].isspace():
            run = 0
        elif text:
            continues = KATAKANA.fullmatch(text[-1]) or text[-1] == 'ー'
            run = run + 1 if continues else 0
    return (doc, decoder, run, text, position + 1), value

"""Markdown markup v8: closing markers of emphasis, code spans, bold, and table pipes.

The component fires on the token that CLOSES a piece of markdown markup in prose:
  * closing `*` (italic, ~2.1) or `**` (bold, ~1.5) opened earlier on the same line
  * closing backtick of an inline code span (`foo`) (~1.4); opening backticks stay near 0
  * a `||` pipe inside a markdown table row (~2.2)
  * heading markers ## / ### (~0.6)
Asterisks used as multiplication, exponent or LaTeX (`3*x`, `x**2`, `align*`) are slightly
negative; everything else is about 0.
"""

CLOSE_BOLD = 1.5         # closing ** of an open bold span
CLOSE_CODE = 1.4         # closing backtick of an inline code span
TABLE_PIPE = 2.2         # || inside a table row
HEADING = 0.6            # ## ### #### ... markers
OPERATOR = -0.25         # unpaired * or ** (multiplication, exponent)
LATEX = -1.0             # \begin{align*}


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    if carry is None:
        carry = {"open": {}, "table": False, "line_start": True}
    tok = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    prev = prefix.token_strings[-2] if len(prefix) > 1 else "\n"
    if "\n" in prev:                       # a new line resets the markup state
        carry["open"] = {}
        carry["line_start"] = True
    if carry["line_start"]:
        carry["table"] = tok.lstrip().startswith("|")
        carry["line_start"] = False
    # a token with a leading space, or after a space/bracket/newline, opens markup
    spaced = tok[:1] == " " or prev[-1:] in ("", " ", "\n", "(", "[", "*")
    value = 0.0
    if tok == "**:":
        value = 0.3
    elif "||" in tok:
        value = TABLE_PIPE if carry["table"] and not spaced else 0.2
    elif "*" in tok:
        marker = "**" if "**" in tok else "*"
        if spaced:
            carry["open"][marker] = True
            value = 0.0
        elif "align" in prev or prev.endswith("{"):
            value = LATEX
        elif carry["open"].get(marker):
            carry["open"][marker] = False
            value = CLOSE_BOLD if marker == "**" else CLOSE_ITALIC
        else:
            value = OPERATOR

        value = 0.2 if spaced else CLOSE_CODE

Almost always near zero. It fires on a few recognisable spots, in two families.

Positive: JavaScript / Node module syntax.
  * the "./" that opens a relative file path after `from`, `require(` or `import`
  * `default`, `const`, `function` right after `export`
  * `.exports` after `module`, and `=` after `module.exports`
  * `dirname` / `DIR` / `FILE` in `__dirname`, `__DIR__`, `__FILE__`
  * `const` or `export` opening a line after a blank line (top-level declarations)

  * the space (or `of`) right after a day ordinal such as "1st", "24th":
    "Feb 1st [ ]2020", "47th [ ]48", "the 10th [of] February"
  * `of` right after `first` / `last`
  * `possible` after a superlative: "all possible", "largest possible"
  * `solid` after `px` (CSS border: 2px solid)
  * the colon in a "Title:" line

The first token of each document is slightly negative (about -0.1 on average; it depends
only on the token itself, since the model sees nothing before it).
Everything else predicts 0. The program reads only the current token and the few before
it, so it is causal. Its values are the mean activations of each group in training text.

SUPERLATIVES = (" all", " best", " largest", " smallest", " highest", " maximum",
                " minimal", " each", " next", " minimum")

    prev = tokens[-2] if len(tokens) > 1 else ""

        return carry, -0.12                # first token of a document: slightly negative

    if cur == " " and prev in ORDINAL_SUFFIXES and prev2.isdigit():
        return carry, -6.0                 # "Feb 1st [ ]2020"
    if c == "of" and prev in ORDINAL_SUFFIXES and prev2.isdigit():
        return carry, -4.5                 # "the 10th [of] February"
    if c == "possible" and prev in SUPERLATIVES:
        return carry, -4.0                 # "all [possible]"
    if c == "of" and prev in FIRST_LAST:
        return carry, -3.0                 # "First [of] all"
    if c == "solid" and p == "px":
        return carry, -9.0                 # "2px [solid]"
    if c == ":" and p == "Title":
        return carry, -2.0                 # "Title[:]"

    # Positive: JavaScript / Node module syntax.
    if cur.endswith("./") and "../" not in cur and p in MODULE_SPACE_WORDS:
        return carry, 4.0                  # from "./..., require('./...
    if c in ("dirname", "DIR", "FILE") and prev.endswith("__"):
        return carry, 6.0                  # __dirname, __DIR__
    if c == ".exports" and p == "module":
        return carry, 6.0                  # module[.exports]
    if c == "=" and p == ".exports":
        return carry, 4.5                  # module.exports[ =]
    if c == "default" and p == "export":
        return carry, 7.0                  # export [default]
    if c == "function" and p == "default":
        return carry, 7.0                  # export default [function]
    if c in ("const", "function") and p == "export":
        return carry, 4.0                  # export [const]
    if c == "export" and prev.endswith("\n\n"):
        return carry, 2.0                  # top-level export after a blank line
    if c == "const" and prev.endswith("\n\n"):
        return carry, 2.0                  # top-level const after a blank line
    return carry, 0.0

"""Activation of layers.1.mlp.down_proj:3853, predicted from the text alone.

This component is a mostly-silent unit that turns strongly negative in three
situations, and is near zero everywhere else:

1. Line-number gutters. In a numbered listing of code (as printed by `cat -n`
   or a file viewer), a line looks like "   262<TAB>    code". The TAB token
   that follows a line number is strongly negative; the more indentation after
   it, the stronger the response (bare tab about -0.95, tab plus spaces about -1.6).
   With a one-digit line number it is weaker (about -0.8).
2. Indentation after an escaped newline. Code embedded in a JSON or string
   literal shows line breaks as a backslash followed by "n". The spaces that
   follow that "\\n" are strongly negative (about -1.3).
3. Years. The second digit of a number starting with 19 or 20 is negative:
   the "9" of "19xx" (about -0.7) and the "0" of "20xx" (about -0.5).

Everything else predicts 0. Ordinary words and punctuation are not predicted.
"""

import re

READS = ()


def isdig(s):
    return len(s) == 1 and s in "0123456789"


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    toks = prefix.token_strings
    t = prefix.position
    s = toks[t]  # the token being predicted
    p = toks[t - 1] if t >= 1 else ""  # the token before it
    pp = toks[t - 2] if t >= 2 else ""  # two tokens before it

    # 1. A tab (optionally followed by indentation) right after a line number.
    if re.fullmatch(r"\t[ \t]*", s) and isdig(p):
        if not isdig(pp):
            return None, -0.8
        return None, (-0.95 if s == "\t" else -1.6)

    # 2. Indentation right after an escaped newline (a backslash and an n).
    if re.fullmatch(r"[ \t]+", s) and (pp + p).endswith("\\n"):
        return None, -1.35

    # 3. Second digit of a year: "9" after a leading "1", "0" after a leading "2".
    if isdig(s) and isdig(p) and not isdig(pp):
        if s == "9" and p == "1":
            return None, -0.7
        if s == "0" and p == "2":
            return None, -0.5

    return None, 0.0

    value -= .180 * linebreak * (family == 2 and kind not in ('colon', 'brace'))

    if re.match(r'^\s', token):

    else:
        parts = 0
    if ((kind in WORD_CLASSES and not kind.startswith('foreign')) or kind in
            ('comma', 'period', 'colon', 'semicolon', 'newline')):
        span_length = 0
    else:
        span_length += 1
    history = (history + ((uppercase, punctuation),))[-8:]
    return (doc, token, previous, parts, span_length, history), float(value)

  * "main" right after "func"                           -> about -3
  * "com" / "org" right after "package" (Java names)    -> about -4
  * "for" right after "you" (as in "thank you for")     -> about -2.5
  * "for" right after "Thanks"                          -> about -2
  * "to" right after "Welcome"                          -> about -4.5
  * "name" right after "my"                             -> about -2
  * "php" right after "<?"                              -> about -5

document starting) and on the newline that follows "<|im_start|>user" (about +0.3).
Everything else predicts 0.

    ("package", "main"): -12.0,
    ("func", "main"): -3.0,
    ("package", "com"): -4.0,
    ("package", "org"): -4.0,
    ("you", "for"): -2.5,
    ("Thanks", "for"): -2.0,
    ("Welcome", "to"): -4.5,
    ("my", "name"): -2.0,

The component is near zero almost everywhere. It does three things:
1. It goes negative on the first token the model sees in a document (the token
   right after <|endoftext|>, or the first token of a packed row). With no earlier
   context there, the token's own identity sets the value: about -0.2 on average,
   a little positive when the token is a digit, and -7.3 when that first token is
   <|endoftext|> itself.
2. It goes to about -0.52 on the doubled middle dot token "··", wherever it occurs.
3. It goes to about -1.6 on the colon of a "Title:" at the start of a document.
Everything else is predicted as 0.
"""

READS = ()

EOT = "<|endoftext|>"
DOUBLE_MIDDLE_DOT = "··"


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    n = len(prefix)
    doc_start = n == 1 or prefix.document_ids[-2] != prefix.document_ids[-1]
    if doc_start:
        if n == 1 and token == EOT:
            return carry, -7.3
        if token.strip().isdigit():
            return carry, 0.1
        return carry, -0.25
    if token == DOUBLE_MIDDLE_DOT:

    if token == ":" and prefix.token_strings[-2] == "Title" and title_start:
        return carry, -1.6
    return carry, 0.0

"""A spelling-and-local-grammar approximation to the with/possession response.

English 'with' gives a negative pulse. Commas, opening brackets, mathematical
notation and polygon names strengthen it; conventional with-complements and
relational words weaken it. Capitalized 'With' has a fixed response. Forms of
'have' get smaller pulses, weakened after personal pronouns and person nouns.
A small spelling dictionary covers other languages' with/possession forms.
These are local heuristics, not a syntactic or semantic parser.
"""
import re
from functools import lru_cache
import wordnet

READS = ()

# Conventional with-complements, rather than a newly introduced description.
COMPLEMENTS = set('''
associate connect link couple pair combine unite join collaborate cooperate
interact communicate speak talk meet consult cope deal struggle wrestle
bother trouble problem issue difficulty familiar comfortable uncomfortable
satisfied dissatisfied pleased delighted obsessed content concerned
impressed disappointed fill cover coat paint treat charge equip arm supply
endow share align accompany affiliate identify relate involve engage
confront face accordance conjunction association connection touch odds
along up start begin work
'''.split())

# Relations that intrinsically compare, connect, or bring two things together.
RELATIONS = set('''
agree disagree comply accord conform correspond coincide match compare
contrast correlate vary increase decrease interfere conflict collide mix
blend merge replace substitute border contact compatibility incompatible
compatible consistency consistent identical congruent satisfaction
'''.split())

PERSONAL = set('''
i you he she we they who someone somebody nobody anyone everyone
'''.split())
NONPERSONAL = set('it this that which these those each'.split())
MODALS = set('can could would should might may must'.split())

# These are words or prepositional prefixes, not arbitrary vocabulary IDs.
OTHER_FORMS = {
    ' с': -2.35, ' со': -2.3, 'с': -.3, ' С': -.75, 'С': -1.2,
    ' con': -1.45, ' Con': -.35, ' com': -1.1, ' Com': -1.1,
    'Com': -.5, ' mit': -1.9, ' avec': -2.0, ' Avec': -3.0,
    ' cu': -.8, ' med': -1.2, ' dengan': -2.3, ' với': -2.3,
    ' có': -1.7, ' ب': -.95, ' بال': -1.35, ' بك': -1.6,
    '与': -.9, '與': -.9, ' без': -1.0,
}

@lru_cache(maxsize=8192)
def lexical(word):
    pos = wordnet.parts_of_speech(word)
    cats = wordnet.categories(word)
    bases = set(wordnet.base_forms(word)) | {word}
    polygon = wordnet.is_a(word, 'polygon')
    return pos, cats, bases, polygon


def predict(token, previous):
    word = token.strip().lower()
    if word not in {'with', 'have', 'has', 'having', 'had', 'without'}:
        if re.fullmatch(r'[_-][Ww]ith', token):
            return -1.8
        return OTHER_FORMS.get(token, 0.0)
    if word == 'without':
        return -.4
    if word == 'had':
        return -.18
    match = re.search(r'([A-Za-z]+)\W*$', previous)
    last = match.group(1).lower() if match else ''
    pos, cats, bases, polygon = lexical(last)
    if word == 'with':
        if token.strip() != 'with':
            return -2.2
        end = previous.rstrip()
        if end.endswith(','):
            return -5.3
        if last == 'but':
            return -4.6
        if end.endswith(('(', '[', '{')):
            return -4.0
        if re.search(r'(?:\\\)|\\\]|\$)\s*$', previous):
            return -3.8
        if polygon:
            return -5.0
        if bases & RELATIONS:
            return 0.0
        if bases & COMPLEMENTS:
            return -.8
        if last in {'and', 'or'}:
            return -2.4
        if 'verb' in pos:
            return -1.3
        return -2.2
    if last in PERSONAL:
        return 0.0
    if last in MODALS or re.search(r'\d\W*$', previous):
        return -1.2
    if last in NONPERSONAL:
        return -.9
    if 'noun.person' in cats:
        return -.2
    if cats & {'noun.artifact', 'noun.body', 'noun.shape'}:
        return -1.0
    return -.6 if word == 'has' else -.4


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    document = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    previous = carry[1] if carry is not None and carry[0] == document else ''
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    value = predict(token, previous)
    return (document, (previous + token)[-160:]), float(value)

"""layers.1.mlp.down_proj:3861: a detector for name initials, transliterated-name dots and
printf-style format letters.

In plain terms, this component is near zero on almost every token. It switches on at a few
recognisable spots where a name or a format code is in the middle of being written:

1. A period right after a single capital letter, a name's middle initial ("Richard P.",
   "J. K."): about 0.5. Not when the letter starts a line, as in list labels ("\\nD.").
2. A middle dot "·" written straight after a Chinese or Japanese character, the separator
   inside a transliterated foreign name ("布蕾克·卡..."): about 1.9. The double dot "··"
   gives 0.5 and the katakana dot "・" 0.2.
3. The conversion letter of a printf-style code, the "d" in "%d" or the "s" in "%4.4s":
   about 1.0. The letter must follow a '%' with only digits, dots, signs or spaces between.
4. A blank line right after a think tag ("<think>\\n\\n", "</think>\\n\\n"): about 0.37.
   A markdown heading marker "###" right after a blank line: about 0.3.

Every other token is predicted as 0. The values are rough averages of the activation in
each case (measured on training rows). The program is calibrated (fitted slope about 0.93).
It reaches variance explained about 0.16 on eval. A token table would reach about 0.12 on
its own, so these context rules do better than token identity. What they leave out is the
diffuse background (most of the variance) and the document-start tokens, whose value is set
by the token alone.
"""

import unicodedata

READS = ()
FORMAT_FILLER = set("0123456789.-+ #")
MIDDLE_DOT_AFTER_CJK = 1.9
INITIAL_PERIOD = 0.5
FORMAT_LETTER = 1.0
THINK_BLANK_LINE = 0.37
HEADING = 0.3


def _is_cjk_or_kana(ch):
    try:
        name = unicodedata.name(ch)
    except ValueError:
        return False
    return name.startswith(("CJK", "HIRAGANA", "KATAKANA"))


def _is_initial(s):
    s = s.strip()
    return len(s) == 1 and s.isalpha() and s.isupper()


def _inside_format_code(prefix):
    """True if a '%' opens a printf-style code just before the newest token: '%', then
    only digits, dots, signs, '#' or spaces, then the newest token."""
    for back in range(2, 8):
        if len(prefix) < back:
            return False
        t = prefix.token_strings[-back]
        if t.endswith("%"):
            return True
        if not t or not set(t) <= FORMAT_FILLER:
            return False
    return False

    tok = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    prev = prefix.token_strings[-2] if len(prefix) > 1 else ""
    prev2 = prefix.token_strings[-3] if len(prefix) > 2 else ""
    if tok == "·":
        return carry, MIDDLE_DOT_AFTER_CJK if prev and _is_cjk_or_kana(prev[-1]) else 0.0
    if tok == "··":
        return carry, 0.5
    if tok == "・":
        return carry, 0.2
    if tok == "." and _is_initial(prev) and "\n" not in prev2:
        return carry, INITIAL_PERIOD
    if len(tok) == 1 and tok.isalpha() and _inside_format_code(prefix):
        return carry, FORMAT_LETTER
    if tok == "\n\n" and prev in ("<think>", "</think>"):
        return carry, THINK_BLANK_LINE
    if tok == "###" and prev.endswith("\n\n"):

    return carry, 0.0

"""A French-context spelling contrast, approximated from training examples.

A decaying balance of French and English function words (and French accents)
controls the strength. Very common space-prefixed French tokens are left at
zero. Other Latin tokens get a short spelling score: notably positive `ou`,
`ss` and final `d`, versus e-family endings and some prefixes. Punctuation
; : ? ! has opposite signs with and without a space in its token.
This is an orthographic approximation, not a pronunciation model.
"""
from functools import lru_cache
from wordfreq import zipf_frequency

READS = ()
FRENCH = frozenset("""
les des du une dans pour avec sur et est que qui nous vous leur aux au
ces cette dont mais par pas ne plus se ce son ses sont elle elles ils
aussi tout sans
""".split())
ENGLISH = frozenset("""
the of to and in is it that for with as was this on be are by from have
not but at his her he she they we you
""".split())

CONTAINS = {
    'ou': 1.547,
    'on': 0.298,
    'eu': -0.187,
    'ai': -0.072,
    'ee': -1.291,
}

STARTS = {
    're': -0.196,
    'pre': -0.706,
    'att': 0.809,
    'app': -0.902,
}

ENDS = {
    'e': -0.248,
    'ere': -1.004,
    's': -0.209,
    't': 0.061,
    'd': 0.709,
    'r': -0.114,
    'g': 0.197,
    'ss': 0.968,
}


@lru_cache(maxsize=32768)
def token_score(text):
    word = text.strip().lower()
    space = bool(text) and text[0].isspace()
    french = word in FRENCH
    english = word in ENGLISH
    evidence = (float(french) - 0.7 * english
                + 0.8 * any(c in word for c in "éèêàçœ"))
    value = 0.0
    latin = bool(word) and all(
        "a" <= c <= "z" or c in "àâäéèêëîïôöùûüçœ" for c in word)
    if latin:
        fr = zipf_frequency(word, "fr")
        en = zipf_frequency(word, "en")
        if not (space and fr > 5.7):
            n = len(word)
            value = 0.202
            value += -0.096 * space + -0.433 * (n == 1) + -0.21 * (n == 2)
            value += -0.279 * word.count("é")
            value += -0.262 * sum(word.count(c) for c in "àèù")
            value += 0.168 * sum(word.count(c) for c in "âêîôû")
            value += 0.162 * fr / 7 + 0.122 * en / 7
            value += -0.197 * french + -0.071 * english
            value += sum(v for s, v in CONTAINS.items() if s in word)
            value += sum(v for s, v in STARTS.items() if word.startswith(s))
            value += sum(v for s, v in ENDS.items() if word.endswith(s))
    if word in (";", ":", "?", "!"):
        value += 1.427 * (1 if space else -1) + 0.571 * space
    value += 0.409 * ("»" in word)
    value += 0.418 * ("ou" in word and not space)
    return evidence, value


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    document = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    state = 0.0 if carry is None or carry[0] != document else carry[1]
    evidence, value = token_score(prefix.token_strings[-1])
    state = 0.93 * state + evidence
    strength = min(1.0, max(0.0, (state - 0.2) / 2.5))
    return (document, state), float(strength * value)

"""Approximate a mostly negative document-onset signal.

Latin script and alphabetic tokens get stronger negative values; common
English tokens get a frequency bonus. Keep this value through an identical
initial token run, then emit zero. This captures onset and coarse lexical
familiarity, not the component's individual-token peculiarities.

import regex
from wordfreq import zipf_frequency

READS = ()


@lru_cache(maxsize=8192)
def onset(token):
    s = token.strip()
    latin = bool(regex.search(r'\p{Script=Latin}', s))
    commonness = max(0.0, zipf_frequency(s, 'en') - 4.0) if s else 0.0
    return (-1.1928 - 1.8575 * latin - 1.0931 * s.isalpha()
            + 0.9117 * commonness)

    document = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    token = prefix.token_ids[-1]
    if carry is None or document != carry[0]:
        carry = (document, token, True)
    elif token != carry[1]:
        carry = (document, carry[1], False)
    value = onset(prefix.token_strings[-1]) if carry[2] else 0.0
    return carry, value

after a document break, or the first token of a row). There the activation depends only
on which token it is, and it is mostly negative: about -3.5 for an ordinary alphabetic

    '': 0.45,
    'a': 1.20,
    'e': 0.85,
    'i': -0.44,
    'o': -0.09,
    'u': -0.59,
    'other': -0.70,
}

    'an': 1.40,
    'en': -0.72,
    'in': -0.58,
    'on': 0.49,
    'un': 0.42,
}

def romanize(text):
    return anyascii(text).lower()

    before, current = romanize(previous), romanize(token)
    text, boundary = before + current, len(before)
    word = current.strip()
    continued = bool(before[-1:].isalpha() and current[:1].isalpha())
    value, strength = 0.0006, 0.0

        m = matches[-1]

        score += 0.37 * continued + 0.34 * split
        score += 0.53 * (split and preceding_vowel)

           for m in re.finditer('d[aeiou]n', text)):

"""A broad spelling-m detector, including m in transliteration.

Short fragments and internal m's are stronger than word-initial Latin m's.
English common-word frequency and neighboring letters adjust the strength.
The signal can continue onto the next two unspaced fragments.
Chat boundaries, comment openers, long dashes and ellipses get offsets.
This is an approximation, not a token-identity lookup.
"""
import math
import re
from collections import namedtuple
from functools import lru_cache
from anyascii import anyascii
from wordfreq import zipf_frequency

READS = ()
Token = namedtuple('Token', 'score trace initial common starts ends')
EMPTY = Token(0., 0., 0., 0., False, False)

BEFORE_M = {'a': 0.43, 'e': 0.36, 'o': 0.49, 'r': 0.46}

@lru_cache(maxsize=65536)
def spelling(text):
    letters = ''.join(c for c in anyascii(text).lower() if c.isalpha())
    if text.startswith('<|') and text.endswith('|>'):
        letters = ''
    n = max(1, len(letters))
    inv = 1 / math.sqrt(n)
    count = letters.count('m')
    trace = count * inv
    initial = letters.startswith('m') and 'm' in text.lower()
    freq = zipf_frequency(letters, 'en') if count else 0.
    common = bool(count) * max(0, freq-3)
    value = 0.02 + 1.96 * trace
    value += initial * (0.38 - 1.79 * inv)
    value -= 0.4 * max(0, count-1)
    value += 0.76 * (letters == 'm')
    value += 0.18 * (bool(count) and n <= 3)
    value -= 0.3 * bool(count) * max(0, freq-5)
    if 'm' not in text.lower():
        value -= 1.1 * trace
    value += 1.5 * ('/**' in text)
    dash = text.strip() in ('—', '―') or re.fullmatch(r'[-=]{3,}', text.strip())
    value += 0.65 * bool(dash)
    value += 0.43 * ('…' in text or bool(re.fullmatch(r'\.{2,}', text.strip())))
    value += 1.12 * (text == '<|im_start|>')
    value -= 0.1 * (text in ('<|im_end|>', '<|endoftext|>'))
    for i, c in enumerate(letters):
        if c != 'm':
            continue
        if i:
            value += inv * BEFORE_M.get(letters[i-1], 0.)
    return Token(value, trace, initial*inv, common,
                 bool(text) and text[0].isalnum(),
                 bool(text) and text[-1].isalnum())


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    doc = int(prefix.document_ids[-1])
    if carry is None or carry[0] != doc:
        previous, older = EMPTY, EMPTY
    else:
        _, previous, older = carry
    current = spelling(prefix.token_strings[-1])
    value = current.score
    if current.starts:
        value += 0.73 * previous.trace
        value += 0.24 * previous.starts * older.trace
        if previous.ends:
            value += 0.67 * current.initial
            value += 0.15 * current.common
    return (doc, current, previous), float(value)

What it does: this component writes into the residual stream whenever the current
token contains the sound/letter "m". It is nearly silent on everything else. It is
strongest when "m" is a short fragment such as "am", "im", "um", "em", "m", "mm"
(about 1.2), weaker when "m" sits inside a longer word piece such as "some", "time",
"command", "community" (about 0.9), and weak when a longer word merely starts with
"m" such as "make", "may", "most" (about 0.45). The same sound written in other
scripts (Cyrillic м, Greek μ, Arabic م, Thai ม, Katakana マミムメモ, ...) counts too.
Everything else sits near zero.

The program looks only at the current token (its text, decoded alone), so it has
no carry and no look-ahead.
"""

M_SOUND = set("mMмМμΜمムマミメモめまみむ임음ม")

SHORT_PIECE = 1.2  # "am", "im", "um", "m", "mm", " m" ...
INSIDE_WORD = 0.9  # "m" in the middle or end of a longer piece: "some", "time"
WORD_START = 0.45  # a longer piece that starts with m: "make", "may", "most"
OTHER = 0.03  # no m-sound at all


def m_value(token):
    """How strongly one decoded token engages the m-sound feature."""
    text = token.lstrip(" ")  # a leading space marks the start of a word

    return carry, float(m_value(prefix.token_strings[-1]))

pieces of the English word "free" (and its German cousin "frei") as they are
spelled out one token at a time: "fre" / " fre" / "Fre" (strongest), then whole
"free"-words such as " free", " Free", "-free", "FREE", "freely" (moderate),
and weakly on "freedom". Words that merely start with the same letters
("frequency", "fresh", "French") do not trigger it.

The program tracks the word being typed (its letters so far, carried from the
previous token, reset at each new document) and predicts a fixed negative value
for each "free"-family word-so-far.

    """Predicted activation once the word typed so far is `word`."""
    w = word.lower()
    if w in ("fre", "frei"):
        return -7.0            # word-start fragments of "free"/"frei"
    if w.startswith("freedom"):
        return -1.0            # "freedom" responds weakly
    if w.startswith("free"):
        return -3.0            # whole "free", "freely", "-free", "FREE", ...

    word = carry or ""
    if len(prefix.document_ids) > 1 and prefix.document_ids[-2] != prefix.document_ids[-1]:

target. Concretely:

    before it (Eq. \\[eq0:, Figure \\[fig:, Table \\[t1): strong; other \\[ are weak;

    citation openers [@ and ; @;

positions): \\label{ opens at about 19, \\ref{ at about 17, the kind word after either at

    "\\eqref{": (19.0, 12.0),
    "\\ref{": (17.0, 12.0),
    "\\cite{": (10.0, 0.0),
    "{#": (4.0, 12.0),
    'ref-type="': (0.0, 6.0),
    'data-label="': (13.0, 11.0),

CITE_OPENERS = {"[@": 4.0, "; @": 8.0}
# Words that make a following escaped bracket \[ a cross-reference.
REF_WORDS = (
    "eq.", "eqs.", "eq", "fig.", "fig", "figure", "table", "theorem", "lemma",
    "proposition", "section", "sec.", "conjecture", "corollary", "equation", "see", "ref.",
)

KIND_WORDS = {"eq", "equ", "fig", "tab", "sec", "def", "thm", "th", "lem", "prop", "cor"}
END_OF_KEY = "}])\n "
COLON = 13.0
ESCAPED_BRACKET_AFTER_REF = 15.0
ESCAPED_BRACKET_OTHER = 5.0
OTHER_KEY_WORD = 3.0  # an alphabetic word starting a key that is not a kind word


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    if len(prefix.token_ids) > 1 and prefix.document_ids[-1] != prefix.document_ids[-2]:

    tail = "".join(prefix.token_strings[-6:])
    tok = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    # carry: None outside a key, else (activation for a kind word, kind word still due)
    state = carry
    value = 0.0
    key_openers = [o for o in KEY_OPENERS if tail.endswith(o)]
    cite_openers = [o for o in CITE_OPENERS if tail.endswith(o)]
    if key_openers:
        opener = max(key_openers, key=len)
        value, kind_value = KEY_OPENERS[opener]
        state = (kind_value, True)
    elif tail.endswith("\\["):
        before = tail[:-2].rstrip(" (\\\xa0")
        after_ref = before.lower().endswith(REF_WORDS)
        value = ESCAPED_BRACKET_AFTER_REF if after_ref else ESCAPED_BRACKET_OTHER
        state = (12.0, True)
    elif cite_openers:

        else:
            if due and tok in KIND_WORDS:
                value = kind_value
            elif due and tok.isalpha():
                value = OTHER_KEY_WORD
            state = (kind_value, False)
    return state, value

"""layers.1.mlp.down_proj:3891 as a short program.

What it captures: this component goes strongly negative on the piece of an Indonesian
word that comes right after a verb prefix (ber-, ter-, mem-, meng-, men-, di-, ke-, se-,
per-, pe-, ...). Indonesian words are split into several byte-level tokens, e.g.
"ber|bed|a", "mem|ak|ai", "ke|bias|aan", and the component is most negative on the second
piece, less on later pieces. It is weaker when the stem piece is long (a likelier whole
word such as "berikut" or "sejak", which do not fire). It only fires when the recent text
looks Indonesian: at least GATE of the last WINDOW words are common Indonesian function
words. Without the gate, the same rule fires on English words such as "di|rect" and
"me|mory" and predicts badly on ordinary text.

Predicted values are negative magnitudes on the activation scale; all other positions 0.
"""
READS = ()

# Verb prefix -> how strongly the piece after it is pushed negative.
PREFIX_STRENGTH = {
    "ber": 4.0, "ter": 4.0, "mem": 4.0, "ke": 4.0, "di": 4.0, "dib": 3.5, "dip": 3.5,
    "meng": 3.0, "men": 3.0, "mel": 2.0, "mer": 3.0, "me": 2.5, "se": 2.0,
    "per": 1.5, "pe": 1.5, "peng": 1.5, "pem": 2.0, "pen": 2.0,
}
# Common Indonesian function words, used as the language cue.
ID_FUNCTION_WORDS = {
    "yang", "dan", "di", "ini", "itu", "dengan", "untuk", "tidak", "dari", "akan",
    "dalam", "adalah", "bisa", "ada", "saya", "kita", "mereka", "juga", "atau", "sudah",
    "oleh", "pada", "karena", "ke", "kamu", "anda", "bahwa", "telah", "dapat", "sebagai",
}
WINDOW = 20   # how many recent words the language cue looks at
GATE = 3      # how many of them must be Indonesian function words
LATER = 0.25  # weight for pieces after the second


def _strength(word):
    """Strength of the verb prefix that the word starts with, else 0."""
    best = 0.0
    for p, s in PREFIX_STRENGTH.items():
        if word.startswith(p):
            best = max(best, s)
    return best


def _length_factor(stem):
    """Short stem fragments fire more than long, probably whole, words."""
    if len(stem) <= 3:
        return 1.0
    if len(stem) == 4:
        return 0.6
    return 0.3


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    tok = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    if carry and carry[0] == doc:
        _, word, pieces, recent = carry
    else:
        word, pieces, recent = "", 0, ()
    core = tok.strip().lower()
    value = 0.0
    if pieces > 0 and tok[:1] != " " and core.isalpha():
        # This token continues the current word.
        word += core
        pieces += 1
        if sum(recent) >= GATE:
            s = _strength(word) * _length_factor(core)
            if pieces == 2:
                value = -s
            elif pieces > 2:
                value = -LATER * s
    elif core.isalpha():
        # A new word starts here; record whether it is an Indonesian function word.
        word, pieces = core, 1
        recent = (recent + (1 if core in ID_FUNCTION_WORDS else 0,))[-WINDOW:]
    else:
        word, pieces = "", 0
    return (doc, word, pieces, recent), value

"""Layer-1 MLP down_proj component 3893: a weak script-of-token detector.

What it does, in plain terms: the component responds to which writing system the
current token is written in. It is near zero on ordinary Latin-alphabet text, digits,
punctuation and spaces. It is clearly positive on tokens written in Arabic, Thai,
Hiragana and Hangul, and on partial UTF-8 byte fragments (pieces of a multi-byte
character split across tokens). Cyrillic, Greek, Katakana and kanji are only weakly
positive.

Just after a document starts, every value is nudged up a little, fading over the
first few dozen tokens.

At the first token of a document (the model resets context at each document
boundary) the picture changes: non-Latin scripts become strongly positive, while
digits and Latin words are negative.

The word 何 ("what") is the one strong, specific trigger: it gets about 0.45.

The numbers are per-script means fitted on a sample of training rows; this is not a
per-token table. Honest scope: the component's activation is mostly small,
token-specific noise (std about 0.05), so this program explains only about 1.5% of
its variance. Its end-to-end effect on the model is negligible.
"""

import math
import unicodedata

READS = ()

# Mean activation per writing system: (inside a document, first token of a document).
SCRIPTS = {
    "HIRAGANA": (0.07, 0.3),
    "ARABIC": (0.06, 0.25),
    "THAI": (0.05, 0.25),
    "HANGUL": (0.03, 0.3),
    "KATAKANA": (0.03, 0.0),
    "CYRILLIC": (0.013, 0.03),
    "GREEK": (0.02, 0.15),
    "CJK": (0.007, -0.1),
    "OTHER_LETTER": (0.01, 0.1),
    "LATIN": (0.004, -0.04),
    "PARTIAL": (0.023, -0.03),
    "DIGIT": (0.0, -0.1),
    "PUNCT": (0.0, 0.02),
}


def script_of(text):
    """Writing system of one token, decoded alone."""
    if "�" in text:
        return "PARTIAL"
    letters = [c for c in text if c.isalpha()]
    if not letters:
        return "DIGIT" if any(c.isdigit() for c in text) else "PUNCT"
    c = letters[0]
    if ord(c) < 128:
        return "LATIN"
    name = unicodedata.name(c, "")
    for script in SCRIPTS:
        if script in name:
            return script
    return "OTHER_LETTER"


# The Japanese word 何 ("what"/"some") is the strongest single trigger in the harvest.
NANI = "何"


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    doc = prefix.document_ids
    first = len(doc) == 1 or doc[-1] != doc[-2]
    # Tokens since this document started (0 at its first token), carried along the row.
    distance = 0 if first else carry + 1
    text = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    mid, start = SCRIPTS[script_of(text)]
    if text == NANI:
        mid = start = 0.45
    if first:
        return distance, start
    # Early in a document the mean is a little higher; the bump fades over ~40 tokens.
    return distance, mid + 0.015 * math.exp(-distance / 40.0)

Inside a document, a digit from 0 to 5 directly after an ASCII letter gets a
positive response. Space-separated numbers do not. At document starts the
response is instead a negative baseline, stronger for bare lowercase initials
and longer unspaced ASCII words. These coarse rules leave lexical quirks out.

def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    document = prefix.document_ids[-1]

        value = -0.35

"""Layer 1 MLP down-projection component 3894: a document-start feature.

What it does, in plain terms:
- Its strongest response is at the first token of each document (the position where
  the model's attention and position count restart). There the value is negative for
  most tokens, more negative for a single-character token (a lone letter, digit or
  symbol) than for a longer word, and it is a fixed value per token.
- Inside a document it is nearly silent (noise of about 0.05). The one consistent
  positive response is a digit 0, 1 or 2 written directly after a letter, as in
  identifiers such as `h1`, `addr2` or `df1`.

This program predicts those group averages. It ignores which exact token started the
document, which is the part a per-token table would add (about 0.46 variance explained
on held-out rows with the full table, against about 0.09 for these groups).
"""

READS = ()

START_SINGLE = -0.42  # first token of a document, one character long
START_OTHER = -0.34  # first token of a document, longer
DIGIT_AFTER_LETTER = 0.13  # a digit glued to a letter, inside a document


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    t = prefix.position
    token = prefix.token_strings[t].strip()
    first = t == 0 or prefix.document_ids[t] != prefix.document_ids[t - 1]
    if first:
        return None, START_SINGLE if len(token) == 1 else START_OTHER
    previous = prefix.token_strings[t - 1]
    if token in ("0", "1", "2") and previous[-1:].isalpha():
        return None, DIGIT_AFTER_LETTER
    return None, 0.0

"""Component layers.1.mlp.down_proj:3895: a social-media hashtag-marker detector.

What it does, in plain terms:
- It fires on the "#" symbol when that symbol opens a hashtag inside running text
  (e.g. "... great trip #travel #quotes"). The activation grows with the number of
  hashtags just before it: a first hashtag is weak, a second or later one is strong.
- It stays quiet on a "#" that starts a line or follows indentation (code comments,
  markdown headers, #include), where the activation is about zero.
- Everything else is predicted as 0.

It reads only the tokens up to the current position, and it counts hashtags only
within the same document. Hashtags that come from the "#" in code comments
are gated out by the indentation/line-start rule, but "# comment" after code
on the same line still gets through sometimes, which is one of its errors.
"""

READS = ()

HASH_MARKS = {"#", " #", "##", " ##"}
WINDOW = 10  # how many recent tokens to look back over for earlier hashtags


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    strings = prefix.token_strings
    if strings[-1] not in HASH_MARKS:
        return carry, 0.0

    # The tokens before this one in the same document, newest first.
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    before = []
    for i in range(len(prefix.token_ids) - 2, -1, -1):
        if prefix.document_ids[i] != doc:
            break
        before.append(i)

    # A "#" right after whitespace or at the start of a line is not a hashtag.
    previous = strings[before[0]] if before else ""
    if previous == "" or previous[-1] in " \t\n":
        return carry, 0.0
    line = []
    for i in before:
        if "\n" in strings[i]:
            break
        line.append(strings[i])
    if "".join(reversed(line))[:1] in (" ", "\t"):
        return carry, 0.0

    # How many hashtags came just before it.
    earlier = sum(1 for i in before[:WINDOW] if strings[i] in HASH_MARKS)
    if earlier == 0:
        return carry, 0.5
    if earlier == 1:
        return carry, 2.0
    return carry, 3.7

"""layers.1.mlp.down_proj:3896 - a document-start word detector.

What it does, in plain terms:
  The component is silent almost everywhere. It only speaks at the first token of a
  document (the token right after <|endoftext|>, or the first token of a row). There
  its output depends on which word starts the document, and the sign is word-specific:
    - words about classes, kinds, types and objects (class, struct, protocol, message,
      serialized, entity, toy, "one (classifier)", "many", ...) push it strongly negative;
    - other computing-type words (type, data, error, invalid, ...) push it mildly negative;
    - Latin-style adjectives ending in -al/-ally/-ical/-ional (official, typical,
      financial, physically, ...) push it mildly positive.
  Everywhere else, and for any other word, it predicts 0.

  This is a coarse concept summary. The true value is a per-word lookup with no short
  rule behind it, so this program captures only the largest concept-level trends.

READS = ()

CLASS_WORDS = ("class", "struct", "proto", "msg", "message", "serializ", "entity", "toy")
TYPE_WORDS = ("type", "data", "err", "fault", "invalid", "incorrect", "bug")
ADJECTIVE_ENDINGS = ("ally", "ical", "ional", "ial")


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    t = prefix.position
    starts_document = t == 0 or prefix.document_ids[-1] != prefix.document_ids[-2]

        return carry, 0.0
    word = prefix.token_strings[-1].strip().lower()

    if any(stem in word for stem in TYPE_WORDS):
        return carry, -1.5
    if word.endswith(ADJECTIVE_ENDINGS):
        return carry, 1.3
    return carry, 0.0

1. A "###" token that opens a line right after a blank line (a paragraph break)

   markdown-style section heading appearing in plain text (scraped pages,
   textbooks, lecture notes). The more breaks already seen in the document, the
   more negative: about -0.4 per earlier break, capped at -3.5. Other "###"
   tokens predict 0.
2. The blank line right after a closing "</think>" tag in a chat reply: a
   mild -0.3.

READS = ()

HEADING = "###"
BREAK = "\n\n"
THINK_END = "</think>"
PER_BREAK = 0.4
CAP = 3.5
AFTER_THINK = -0.3


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    # carry: (document id, paragraph breaks so far in that document), or None.
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    breaks = 0

What it does: it goes negative on the word that follows a proper name (a person,
place, organisation, title, or a name followed by a number such as "Windows 2000")
in running prose, i.e. in a sentence rather than a heading or all-caps title.
The strongest response is to a lowercase preposition, conjunction or relative word
right after a multi-word name ("Castleford's 10-5 victory over Bradford Northern [in]",
"Anne Askew [and]"). A comma right after a name gets a smaller negative value, and
any other word or punctuation after a multi-word name gets a faint one. Everywhere
else it predicts 0. A capitalised "In" or "And" after a name does not count.

Why: in the harvest, the component's large negative activations sit right after
a name. Prepositions and conjunctions ("in", "at", "for", "during", "who", "and",

multi-word names. Most of the variance is spread over many small values, so this
captures only part of it (about 0.08 variance explained on eval).

document's text, and resets at each document boundary. A "name word" is a word whose
first letter is capitalised (after stripping quotes and brackets) or that contains a
digit. A name run is the number of name words ending the text just before the
current token, and zero if that text ends in a space. "In prose" means the current
line has at least one word starting with a lowercase letter.

READS = ()

    "in at on for from during before under through after who which that as and or".split()
)

def is_name_word(word):
    """Capitalised or numbered word: the kind of word a name is made of."""
    core = word.strip(PUNCT)
    return core[:1].isupper() or any(ch.isdigit() for ch in core)


def name_run(text):
    """How many name words end `text`; zero if it ends in a space."""
    if not text or text[-1].isspace():
        return 0
    run = 0
    for word in reversed(text.split()):
        if not is_name_word(word):
            break
        run += 1
    return run


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    tail = "" if carry is None else carry
    if len(prefix.document_ids) > 1 and prefix.document_ids[-1] != prefix.document_ids[-2]:
        tail = ""
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    word = token.strip()  # case kept: "In" or "And" starting a line is not the same thing
    line = tail.split("\n")[-1]
    in_prose = any(w[:1].islower() for w in line.split())
    run = name_run(tail)
    value = 0.0
    if run and in_prose and word:
        multi = run >= 2
        if word in PREPOSITIONS:
            value = -0.45 if multi else -0.15
        elif word == ",":
            value = -0.2 if multi else -0.08
        elif multi:
            value = -0.03
    return (tail + token)[-TAIL_CHARS:], value

"""A coarse lexical proxy for names, plus document-boundary effects.

Capitalized, less ordinary words and geographical names get small positive
values; familiar lower-case text stays near zero. Joined ASCII word pieces
allow some split names to be recognized. The initial metadata label 'Title:' has
its own large response. The '.com' suffix gets a small boost, while
'Okay' and 'Alright' get a negative value. Individual entities are not memorized.
"""
from functools import lru_cache
import wordnet
import wordfreq
import pycountry

READS = ()
PLACES = {x.name.casefold() for x in pycountry.countries}
PLACES.update(x.name.casefold() for x in pycountry.subdivisions)


@lru_cache(maxsize=65536)
def lexical(word):
    categories = wordnet.categories(word)
    ordinary = bool(categories - {'noun.person', 'noun.location'})
    place = 'noun.location' in categories or word.casefold() in PLACES
    return wordfreq.zipf_frequency(word, 'en'), bool(categories), ordinary, place


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    start = carry is None or carry[0] != doc
    if start:
        previous, word, position = '', '', 0
    else:
        _, previous, word, position = carry
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    text = token.strip()
    letters = text.isascii() and text.isalpha()
    title = letters and len(text) > 1 and text.istitle()
    space = bool(token and token[0].isspace())
    continued = letters and not space and bool(word)
    joined = word + text if continued else text
    value = -0.005 + 0.005 * space
    if start:
        value -= 0.08 + 0.075 * title
    if title:
        frequency, known, ordinary, place = lexical(text)
        rarity = max(0.0, 5.0 - frequency) / 5.0
        value += 0.08 + 0.085 * rarity + 0.04 * place
        value -= 0.09 * ordinary
        if not known:
            value -= 0.07 + 0.07 * rarity
            if 3 <= frequency < 5:
                value += 0.04
    if continued:
        frequency, known, ordinary, place = lexical(joined)
        if not ordinary and 2.5 < frequency < 5 and len(joined) > 3:
            value += 0.04
    if text == '.com':
        value += 0.12
    if text in {'Okay', 'Alright'}:
        value = -0.11
    if position == 1 and previous == 'Title' and token == ':':
        value = 4.548
    carry = (doc, token, joined if letters else '', position + 1)
    return carry, float(value)

"""Layer 1 MLP down_proj, component 3903: a detector for scraped web boilerplate.

In plain terms: this component is nearly silent on ordinary text. Its clearest responses are
to the stock wording that document-sharing and scraped web pages put around their text:

- the teaser "This preview shows pages 1-3. Sign up to view the full document" and
  "View Full Document": the content words (preview, pages, document, content, words) go
  strongly negative, about -2 to -5 (pages and preview are the strongest);
- a few other stock phrases ("This article is originally from", "full-text version",
  "Download or read book", "Uploaded by") give a milder negative on their content words;
- a form-feed page-break character goes to about -1.2;
- "N months ago" and "N views" listing metadata go mildly negative.

Two weak but steady responses: the URL separator "://" is about +0.25, and the word " line"
in a Python traceback ('File "x.py", line 56') is about +0.85. Everything else is predicted
as 0; most of the component's variance is small token-level noise that no short rule captures.
"""
import re

READS = ()
KEEP = 120  # characters of recent text carried from one position to the next

# Stock phrases that mark scraped boilerplate; a content word after one of them is a response.
BOILERPLATE = ("preview", "Sign up to view", "View Full", "originally", "Download or",
               "full-text", "Uploaded")

# Content words of that boilerplate, with their typical activation.
WORDS = {" preview": -4.0, " pages": -5.0, " shows": -1.5, " document": -2.0,
         " Document": -2.0, " content": -2.0, " words": -2.0, " version": -2.0}


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    """Activation at the newest token, given the text before it in the same document."""
    tok = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    before = carry[0] if carry is not None and carry[1] == doc else ""  # reset per document
    boilerplate = any(phrase in before[-100:] for phrase in BOILERPLATE)
    v = 0.0
    if tok in WORDS and boilerplate:
        v = WORDS[tok]
    elif tok.strip().isdigit() and boilerplate and re.search(r"(pages|Page) $", before):
        v = -1.5  # the "1" in "pages 1-3" or "Page 1 of"
    elif tok == " preview" and before.endswith("This"):
        v = -4.0
    elif tok == "\x0c":
        v = -1.2  # form-feed page break
    elif tok == " line" and before[-40:].endswith('.py",'):
        v = 0.85  # traceback line number
    elif tok == "://":
        v = 0.25
    elif tok == " views" and re.search(r"\d$", before):
        v = -0.5
    elif tok == " ago" and re.search(r"\d+ (day|week|month|year|hour)s?$", before):
        v = -0.7
    text = (before + tok)[-KEEP:]
    return (text, doc), float(v)
